output.question: What did Snowflake say about consumption trends on its most recent earnings call?
output.answer: On its latest earnings call identified as of November 10, 2026—September 2, 2026, for Q2 FY2027—Snowflake said consumption momentum was strengthening, supported by its core data platform and a meaningful increase in AI revenue. Product revenue grew 37% year over year to $1.49 billion in the quarter ended July 31, 2026, its third consecutive quarter of growth acceleration. Management described the acceleration as broad-based rather than concentrated in AI-native companies, and said customers adopting AI were also consuming more of the core platform. Based on observed consumption patterns—not a change in forecasting methodology—Snowflake raised FY2027 product-revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, or 36% growth, on September 2, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Snowflake held its Q2 FY2027 earnings call on September 2, 2026; this was the latest earnings call identified as of November 10, 2026.
For the quarter ended July 31, 2026, product revenue was $1.49 billion, up 37% year over year, marking the third consecutive quarter of growth acceleration.
Management attributed accelerating growth to strength in the core data platform and a meaningful step-up in AI revenue.
Management said acceleration spanned a broad customer base, was not concentrated in AI-native companies, and included increased core-platform consumption among AI adopters.
The CFO said guidance remained based on observed consumption patterns, with no change in forecasting methodology or guidance philosophy.
As of September 2, 2026, FY2027 product-revenue guidance was raised to $6.07 billion, representing 36% year-over-year growth.
